clue.text: Returned to show off clothes

indicators.note: returned means the word for showing off is read backwards, right to left

parts.note: to show off is to brag

explanation.surface: Someone came back just to parade their new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns BRAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is attire, a general word for what someone wears.

clue.text: Understands, whichever way it's put

indicators.note: whichever way the letters are put, forwards or backwards, they read the same: a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A person grasps the point however it is phrased.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, signalled by 'whichever way it's put'.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp or comprehend it.

clue.text: Fat man in exemplary turn-around

indicators.note: in places the word for a man inside the other piece
turn-around says the abbreviation for exemplary is written backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, as in exemplary
HE is a male pronoun, so a man

explanation.surface: An overweight man performs an exemplary about-face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exemplary' stands for e.g.; 'turn-around' flips it, and 'in' sets the man inside the flipped pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is clarified butter, a cooking fat used in South Asian food.

clue.text: Principal thoroughfare in North London

parts.note: arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy
a way is a road or thoroughfare

explanation.surface: The main road running through north London.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCHWAY is a district of north London, on the A1 road; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Archway is a named neighbourhood in the northern part of the capital.

clue.text: No one gets charged for disorderly conduct

definitions.meaning: nobody pays: entry costs nothing to everybody
a chaotic brawl or scramble with no rules

explanation.surface: Nobody faces charges over a bout of rowdy behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' looks like police charges, but the first sense is about paying.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both open to everyone at no cost and an uncontrolled melee.

clue.text: Accept current command

parts.note: to accept something is to take it
electric current is a flow of charge

explanation.surface: Agree to assume the present leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: To command a situation is to assume control of it.

clue.text: Plain talking about hire-purchase

parts.note: plain, meaning simple or straightforward, gives easy
terms are words or expressions used in talking

explanation.surface: Frank discussion about buying goods on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word. Hire-purchase is the British name for buying by instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Instalment buying is sold as paying on gentle, spread-out conditions.

clue.text: Manage to get something to eat

definitions.meaning: to ... is to get on or manage, as in how did you ...

explanation.surface: Contrive to find a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: getting along, and the food served.

clue.text: Right to vote for his inclusion in EC country

indicators.note: inclusion in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: France was a member of the European Community

explanation.surface: A man campaigns to win suffrage for his own entry into a European state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; the EC was the European Community, forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the legal entitlement to cast a ballot.

clue.text: Pleads for trees to be planted around the Home Counties

indicators.note: the trees are planted around the other piece, so it goes inside them

parts.note: beeches are trees
the Home Counties are the counties around London in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: Someone begs for trees to be put in across the counties surrounding London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London; 'for' and 'to be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg or implore earnestly.

clue.text: Lamb's mother was a Ghanaian

definitions.meaning: the mother of a lamb is a female sheep
a member of a West African people living in Ghana and Togo

explanation.surface: A lamb's mum turns out to have been from West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a female sheep and also a West African people of Ghana.

clue.text: An affirmation from those who vote affirmatively

definitions.text: An affirmation from those who vote affirmatively

parts.words: An affirmation from those who vote affirmatively
parts.note: the cry of yes from voters in favour, as in a parliamentary division

explanation.surface: A yes from the people backing the motion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament those in favour call out yes in the old form, and are counted as such.

clue.text: That is the difference between colon and colony

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for that, over there

definitions.text: the difference between colon and colony
definitions.meaning: read as ...: putting a ... the end turns one word into the other

explanation.surface: A remark on what separates a punctuation mark from a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. The second sense is read as two words: add a Y on to the first to get the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Yon is a dialect or poetic word meaning that or yonder.

clue.text: Attentive domestic follows former student

indicators.note: follows puts the domestic after the former student

parts.note: OB, old boy, a former pupil
a domestic is a household servant

explanation.surface: A diligent house servant comes after an old pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means watchful, noticing things carefully.

clue.text: Not being linked to German exchange rate is wrong

definitions.text: Not being linked to German exchange rate
definitions.meaning: read literally as off the Deutschmark, no longer pegged to it

explanation.surface: Uncoupling from the German currency is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The mark was Germany's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Off the mark means inaccurate; literally it means detached from the German currency.

clue.text: Lively agent takes in both Right and Left

indicators.note: takes in says the agent's word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A nimble spy absorbs both political wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both' is a link. Right is given in full, Left as L.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means spry and energetic.

clue.text: Bump into and drive over

definitions.meaning: to cross from one side to the other

explanation.surface: Meet by chance, and run someone down with a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means meet unexpectedly and also cross a space.

clue.text: He caters for a business house quite well

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business house
OK means all right, quite well

explanation.surface: A man looks after a firm's food reasonably well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook prepares the food served to others.

clue.text: A fine facade, despite insulting comment

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a facade is the front of a building

explanation.surface: A handsome building face survives a rude remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despite' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an open insult or slight.

clue.text: A royal pretender is coming

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
a pretender to a throne is a rival claimant

explanation.surface: A claimant to the crown is on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; coming here is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of reaching a place, its advent.

clue.text: Greek philosopher takes on a military unit

parts.note: Plato was a philosopher of ancient Athens

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker enlists in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small army subdivision under a lieutenant.

clue.text: He's rough, tough, loveless, confused

indicators.note: confused says the remaining letters are jumbled
loveless means without O, which stands for love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A list of words describing a hard, lonely, muddled man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' takes O from TOUGH, leaving TUGH; 'confused' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent ruffian, a rough character.

clue.text: Heartless incantation which can chill the blood

parts.note: heartless means unfeeling or cold
an incantation is a magic spell

explanation.surface: A cruel curse that makes the blood run cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a period of icy weather chills you to the core.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of freezing weather is a stretch of low temperatures that chill people through.

clue.text: Go for tax-exempt investment

definitions.meaning: energy or vigour, as in full of go
a Personal Equity Plan, a former UK tax-free savings scheme

explanation.surface: Opt for a savings scheme free of tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. The investment was a British scheme replaced by ISAs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pep means vim, and it was the acronym for a tax-free equity plan.

clue.text: Woman one finds in Wuthering Heights'

indicators.note: finds in says the letters are found inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A heroine encountered in the Brontë novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is a link; the letters sit inside Wuthering.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to a female person.

clue.text: Issue needing emended item

indicators.note: emended means corrected or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A publication needs a corrected entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give out or discharge.

clue.text: Paramedic serving mashed potatoes to Henry

indicators.note: mashed suggests the potatoes are pulped and rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A medic dishes up mash to a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath is a practitioner of bone and joint manipulation, an allied health worker.

clue.text: Just the one

explanation.surface: Merely a single one.
explanation.definitionFit: Only means merely as an adverb and sole as an adjective.

clue.text: Current measures produced by a body of legislators

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Legislators pass some fresh measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' is a link; MPs are Members of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperes are units for measuring electric current.

clue.text: Listened to pronouncement from a cabinet minister

indicators.note: pronouncement says the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: listened to means heard

explanation.surface: Heard a statement from a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. Douglas Hurd was a British Conservative cabinet minister, Home and Foreign Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas Hurd held senior posts in Thatcher's and Major's governments.

clue.text: Quarrel with priest perpetually

parts.note: Fr, Father, is the title of a priest
ay, or aye, means always

explanation.surface: Someone forever arguing with a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a brawl or noisy dispute.

clue.text: Ruins the wine and others enjoyment, he does

definitions.text: Ruins the wine and others enjoyment, he does

parts.note: ruins means spoils
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks the port and everyone's fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the killjoy as well as building him.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport ruins other people's fun.
